event: A yellow-fever epidemic is attributed to an inadequate and inferior water supply and becomes the occasion for the incorporation
actors: New York City; Aaron Burr and an association of individuals
notes: The causal sentence is the bank's own.

event: The bill incorporating the Manhattan Company is passed with a surplus-capital clause
actors: New York Legislature; Aaron Burr named the moving spirit
notes: Corroborated as a date by a rival publisher's 1853 roll (history l.2405). No charter text on disk.

event: First meeting of directors; Daniel Ludlow chosen president; Aaron Burr present
location: New York City - the house of Edward Barden Innkeeper
notes: The probe quoted the host as '[Rich]ard Barden'; the bytes print 'Edward Barden' (§T.2).

event: A committee is appointed to consider the most proper means of employing the capital of the Company
notes: The decision pivot from water to money (§N).

event: Books open for public subscription to the 2000000 capital stock at 50 par
notes: Par value is the checkable link to the 1808 increase.

event: The water committee is empowered to contract for and bore pine-log pipes
actors: Osgood; John B. Coles; John Stevens
notes: Physical works of the licensed purpose.

event: The corporate seal is described: Oceanus pouring water; 'Seal of the Manhattan Company'
notes: The water purpose sits inside the banking corporation's symbol (§J).

event: The entire 2000000 is subscribed by several thousand persons; the City of New York takes 2000 shares
notes: The first validation signal (§L).

event: The committee reports in favour of opening an office of discount and deposit
notes: The decision that made the licence a bank.

event: The 'Bank' of the Manhattan Company begins business in a bought house on the site of 'the present No. 40 Wall Street'
notes: The first banking transaction day in the corpus; the same phrase also bounds the booklet's print date.

event: The bank's earliest reproduced advertisement: counter hours 10 to 3; signed 'HENRY REMSEN Cashier'; dated September 24; published in the Mercantile Advertiser of October 9
notes: The market interface (§J).

event: Two months after opening a committee is appointed to visit the vaults and examine the cash
notes: Control machinery; the carrier's '106 years later' claim about State law is held Low (§J).

event: The bank commences paying dividends
notes: No independent count exists.

event: All the city banks move temporarily to the Village of Greenwich to escape the fever season and a country office is decided on
notes: Land acquired between the 'Bowery Road' and the East River; 'Mr. Astor proposed verbally to cede eight lots'.

event: A negotiated union of capitals with the New York State Bank of Albany is offered in the Legislature fails to pass and is abandoned
notes: One of the corpus's only rejected-option records (§O).

event: The Legislature reserves 1000 shares to the State and capital rises to 2050000
notes: Both the State and the City 'are still stockholders' - an undated present tense.

event: Branch offices maintained at Utica and Poughkeepsie
notes: Fractional-currency illustration attributed to Utica.

event: Incorporation at Albany for twenty-one years as 'The New York Chemical Manufacturing Company' with an express anti-banking clause
notes: Part III of the same volume prints the fuller name 'without Banking Privileges' (l.5959-5961).

event: The 'full banking charter' of the Chemical line
notes: Which act begins the bank is contested and is not resolved here.

event: Senate passage reported from Albany: Chemical 22 to 8; Fulton 23 to 8; Long Island 26 to 4
notes: A contemporaneous voice inside a retrospective carrier.

event: First business advertisement in the daily papers offering manufactured chemicals
notes: The licensed purpose's launch; a state Medical Society committee's praise follows in the same carrier (§L).

event: Balthazar P. Melick receipts 50000 from the commissioners (10 per cent on capital)
notes: An autograph receipt described not imaged.

event: Melick's oath of office as president attested by W. A. Seely the Bank's notary and lawyer
notes: First named officer of the Chemical line.

event: Greenwich Village works abandoned; riverfront land bought between 32nd and 34th Streets
notes: The purchase price of the new tract is not printed.

event: John Mason becomes a stockholder
notes: 'While not connected with the Bank's organization' (l.918-919): a role, not a founding claim.

event: John Mason becomes president
notes: Held until his death in 1839.

event: Trustees transfer their main energies from manufacturing to establishing the banking house on Broadway
notes: The licensed purpose is effectively stopped (§M.2).

event: The Manhattan Company is one of the banks receiving Government deposits withdrawn from the second United States Bank
notes: A national authority's selection of the house (§L).

event: The first manufacturing site is sold to George W. Tucker for 6000 against 37219 paid
notes: The quantified failure of the origin asset.

event: The water system reaches Bleecker Street with about twenty-five miles of mains supplying 2000 houses
notes: Scale of the licensed purpose at its maximum printed extent.

event: The Bank of the United States fails to renew its charter and ceases operations; the July 1836 specie circular punctures Western speculation
notes: The carrier's own causal framing of the road to 1837.

event: 'THE FINANCIAL STORM OF 1837. All Specie Payments Suspended': the Chemical follows the other twenty city banks; specie 57,661 to 11,383; circulation 266,969 to 194,634; profits 69,068; stock 124 to 98
notes: Written as printed with no popular-panic gloss; a suspension of the CHEMICAL line only (§M.1).

event: The New York Herald announces specie redemption of Chemical five-dollar notes 'to ladies alone' and pledges earliest resumption
evidence_class: CONTEMPORARY OBSERVATION transmitted in a 1913 carrier
notes: The 1837 newspaper voice survives only inside the bank's own history.

event: The State safety-fund rule is described: half per cent of paid-up capital annually held to three per cent for the debts of any insolvent bank
actors: New York Legislature; the Van Buren system
notes: The corpus's first quantified institutional insurance experiment.

event: Death of John Mason; Isaac Jones elected president on 1839-10-01 and John Quentin Jones succeeds Archibald Craig as cashier
notes: The volume prints both dates and the day stays UNKNOWN.

event: The Croton system is completed and the company's water service ends about that time
notes: The licensed purpose closes; the bank continues.

event: Re-charter: 28 subscribers; five original directors including C. V. S. Roosevelt; Desdoity cashier at 1500; Isaac Jones retires
notes: The 21-year term of 1823 expires and is renewed.

event: Directors at 216 Broadway resolve the first dividend of 6 per cent payable 1849-01-02
actors: John Q. Jones (president); J. B. Desdoity (cashier)
notes: Published in the daily papers 1848-12-27; the reversal of Jones's own retention policy (§N).

event: Total dividends for the year are 12 per cent claimed above all twenty-two dividend-paying city banks
notes: The strongest self-reported validation claim for the Chemical line.

event: The Manhattan Company becomes an original member of the New York Clearing House Association (No. 2 in seniority)
notes: Host institution named (§G).

event: A rival's list of the banks of the city of New York prints the Manhattan Company at 1799 April 2 with 2050000
notes: The corpus's second independent origin for the 1799-04-02 charter date.

event: The Ohio Life Insurance and Trust Company fails completely with a paid-up capital of 2000000 and its business is never resumed
notes: The window's demonstration that an institution of this class could disappear.

event: Minute authorising the president to sign the Clearing House agreement refusing interest on deposits
notes: Printed as 'unsound in principle unsafe in practice and contrary to the best interests of both our dealers and ourselves'.

event: An informal directors' meeting decides NOT to suspend specie payments while the city's banks suspend
notes: The best-documented decision in the stage because its alternative is printed (§N).

event: The other New York banks resume; the Chemical having never suspended stands firm; specie rises from 327282 to 666277 by December 5
notes: The only solvency test with a comparative count.

event: Chapter title: 'Hundred Per Cent. Dividends Through the Panic of 73'
notes: A caption only; recorded and not credited (§L).

event: The booklet's own bounds: dividends counted to January 1913; a '106 years later' statute reference; 'the present No. 40 Wall Street' twice; the Irving Press line without a date
notes: No print date is asserted for the booklet.

event: 'History of the Chemical Bank 1823-1913' copyrighted by The Chemical National Bank
